long_biography.plain_text:
Motor Oil's refinery at Agioi Theodoroi became the centre of Vardis Vardinogiannis's business leadership. A Greek Naval Academy graduate and former naval officer, he joined the refinery's top team at its opening and concentrated on energy operations and international markets.

The company repeatedly enlarged its processing capacity, modernised its production units and developed export links under his chairmanship. Vardinogiannis also oversaw the cooperation with Saudi Aramco and Motor Oil's listing on the Athens Exchange, two changes that widened its capital base and international standing. He remained non-executive chair after relinquishing managing-director duties in 2021, serving until his death in 2024.

Inherited and expanded therefore captures both the material family platform and Vardis's documented operating contribution.

Motor Oil refineries, subsidiaries, shipping operations, hotels, media holdings, bank stakes and other group assets belong to listed companies, private holding entities or other family members. They establish the sector, family control and diversification but are not treated as Vardinogiannis's directly owned personal asset inventory or net worth.

The source owner and Wikipedia use Vardinogiannis, while Motor Oil and Forbes generally use Vardinoyannis and the official middle initial appears as I. or J. in English documents. These are established transliteration variants; the dossier preserves the source owner's display name rather than proposing a speculative correction.
